Crypto exchange comparison, from a trader’s seat

Not another affiliate top-10. This compares every major exchange by the things you actually feel mid-trade: how fees eat your PnL, how leverage sets your liquidation, how thin liquidity slips your fills, how funding bleeds a held position — and, just as important, whether the venue can be trusted with your money. Includes an honest look at the KuCoin controversy.

How each factor hits your trade

Before the table — what these numbers mean when real money is on the line.
Fees

Charged on entry and exit, on the full leveraged size. Round-trip a $10k position at 0.05% and you’ve paid $10 before the trade even moves. Scalpers feel this most — a referral fee discount pays for itself fast.

Leverage

Sets how far price can move before you’re liquidated. 100× ≈ 1% away; 500× ≈ 0.2%. A big “max lev” is marketing — what matters is the leverage you use and where your liq price lands.

Liquidity

Thin books = slippage: your market order walks up the ladder and fills worse than you saw. On majors the top venues are near-perfect; on exotic alt-perps even a modest order can move price against you.

Funding rate

Perps charge funding every few hours to peg them to spot. Hold a crowded long and you pay the shorts — a slow bleed that can outweigh a small win. Same funding market-wide, but venues differ slightly.

Liq engine & insurance

How the exchange closes underwater positions. A fair mark price and a fat insurance fund mean fewer unfair wick-outs and less auto-deleveraging (ADL) clawing back your winning trade.

Trust & safety

The one that dwarfs the rest. Great fees mean nothing if you can’t withdraw. Regulation, proof-of-reserves, security record and how the venue treats victims decide whether your balance is really yours.

The KuCoin problem — an honest word

⚠ Why we flag KuCoin

Reported by on-chain investigator ZachXBT, US prosecutors and EU regulators. Presented as public reporting — do your own research.
Jan 2025Pleaded guilty in the US to operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business, agreeing to roughly $300M in penalties and forfeitures; prosecutors said prior AML/KYC failures let suspicious funds move through the platform. KuCoin is banned for US users.
Aug 2025A user reported a $250,000 theft whose funds landed in five KuCoin deposit addresses allegedly opened with purchased “mule” KYC. When a community member spoke out, KuCoin reportedly threatened legal action over “false or unlawful statements.”
Feb 2026Austria’s financial regulator (FMA) barred KuCoin’s EU arm from onboarding new customers after it reportedly lost its key anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance officers.
Apr–May 2026ZachXBT asked KuCoin to explain how $9.5M from a fake Ledger app was laundered through 150+ KuCoin deposit addresses in a single week, and later wrote that the exchange “does not assist victims or law enforcement,” calling the team “complicit” — alleging illicit funds flow freely as long as they generate fees.
None of this means the exchange will vanish tomorrow, and KuCoin disputes the characterizations — but the pattern (a US guilty plea, an EU onboarding ban, unpaid court awards and repeated victim-handling accusations) is exactly the kind of thing that precedes withdrawal problems. Our take: if you use it, keep minimal balances, withdraw profits promptly, and prefer a venue with a cleaner record. Sources: reporting via Cryptopolitan, BanklessTimes, Cryptoadventure and others (2025–2026).

So which exchange should you actually use?

If liquidity and execution are everything — Binance, then Bybit and OKX. If you want to trade without full KYC — Bybit or Bitget for majors, MEXC for cheap fees and new listings (mind the thin books). If you’re learning — Bitget for copy trading, or just paper-trade here first. If you’re in the US or safety comes first — Kraken or Coinbase, accepting fewer markets and lower leverage. If you want markets beyond crypto — Moon covers stocks, forex and commodities alongside crypto with simple up-or-down calls, 24/7 (see the spotlight above). And whatever you pick, the rule that matters more than any fee: don’t store what you can’t afford to lose on any exchange — they are for trading, not custody.
